reasoning: Long, elongated tan/brown necrotic streaks running parallel to leaf veins across multiple corn leaves. This matches Goss's wilt (bacterial wilt caused by Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. nebraskensis) which produces characteristic water-soaked to tan/brown lesions that run the length of the leaf parallel to veins, distinguishable from Southern Corn Leaf Blight (more rectangular, vein-bounded lesions) and Stewart's wilt (pale green/yellow coloration).
